title: Revert plugin redesign starting with the ABI/license check changes
description:
This is a quite big revert going back to the plugin design in use in the last years.
There was a very brief discussion before the plugin API redesign landed and the redesign did not come with a roadmap, a clear scope of the planned changes and most importantly a cost/benefit analysis.

The thread on wireshark-devel started here: https://www.wireshark.org/lists/wireshark-dev/202312/msg00000.html

I would like to reach a broad agreement on the direction and I won't merge this MR until it gets multiple approvals.

There were open questions in the thread and I'll start revisiting them tomorrow.

I think that changing LUA and Plugin API:s has a big chance of impacting our users parhaps more than we imagine. I know for sure that changes in this area has caused me 
manu hours of extra work over the years - with little benefit IMHO. Like the move of directory paths as an example.
Just my 2 cents

> Like the move of directory paths as an example.

I'm not sure what this is referring to but if you are talking about the removal of the X.Y component of the plugin path, I consider that to be a big win also.

The previous file system hierarchy design was motivated by binary compatibility requirements and it was successful at that but reasoning suggests and experience confirms that it is not as intuitive as it could be for end-users.

Also I suspect Windows might benefit from a different (maybe better) naming convention than `DLL.X` but I will wait for further details on that. This is both because I have less experience with Windows and paid less attention to it during development.

Sorry, I'm not on discord, but I would be very interested in understanding what the "DLL.1" issue is.

Any breaking change has some impact and it is a judgement call but I firmly believe any impartial analysis will conclude the impact is tiny (a trivial plugin registration change) compared to the benefits for users and developers.

In this particular case someone was trying to create a plugin for the first time, and it looks like they were trying use a plugin built in master with Wireshark 4.2. The fact that he had something with an unusual filename that didn't work led to a bit of confusion.

Seems pretty benign. Even without any plugin redesign involved that was not going to work and the user probably saved himself some trouble.

Anyway I don't remember where that particular discussion stopped but I think Windows users might prefer a naming convention like `plugin-X.dll` or `plugin.X.dll`.

There are many more benefits but even if they only included the huge usability improvements for end-users of having the new "Install Plugin" GUI feature that alone would be enough to justify it IMHO, compared to such a small cost.

I can imagine that a graphical install plugin feature would be useful and I believe it can be implemented without a major redesign.
For example when a file is dropped on Wireshark's window, Wireshark would detect if the file is a capture or a plugin and in case it is a plugin it could be installed to the right location.
Without redesigning existing plugin file name formats, paths, etc.

Wireshark is a very mature project with many people relying on it in their profession. IMO we should be very careful with redesigning well established user-level parts of it, like the plugin API and filesystem layout, but we can safely extend it in ways not breaking existing use cases.
Interesting with drag'n'drop support for adding plugins, maybe this also works for Lua plugins? Copy the file to the right location and optionally execute "Reload Lua Plugins".

I agree we should be careful and I think I was very careful. That path change is just one piece of the whole thing and it was prompted by persistent reports of users being confused and my own perception of it being an unnecessarily onerous requirement, that I found an elegant way to do without, otherwise I would have preferred to not introduce breaking changes, obviously.

But if people object to that I am fine with reverting this specific change.

> I can imagine that a graphical install plugin feature would be useful and I believe it can be implemented without a major redesign.

If you have a better way to do it then be my guest.

Drag n' drop or a menu entry or both is just a minor UI design side-issue and irrelevant to this MR in my opinion.
It would be (almost) trivial to extend this new plugin install feature to support Lua plugins. Again menu entry or drag n' drop makes zero difference, other that UX/UI considerations obviously.

I'd be OK with keeping the menu entry as well and even extending it to cover Lua plugins. It is reverted in this MR only because it depends on the plugin path and plugin file name changes and I don't have free time to decouple them.

Oh, would you be OK with that? Well, that's certainly a relief.

Seems to be a common theme with you. All the time you can ever find is just to raise a stink because something makes you unhappy as Debian maintainer and hold this project back by a few more years. Too bad.
Discuss it, merge it or close it. The community, myself included, needs to have a resolution on what will happen to the plugin API many of us are already using and depending on.

I agree that this should not be kept open very long, but I could not get the discussion going when I prepared the MR apparently. I'm glad that there was a discussion and it seems it came to a broader agreement.

Well, let me summarize it for you so far, at least my take:

1. @AndersBroman  wants to revert this because change is dangerous, from what I understood of his argument. Also something about someone being surprised/confused/having questions on Discord.

2. @geraldcombs  gave it a thumbs up so that it would suggest that he is in favor of this big revert of 2+ weeks of my work (which is a continuation of all that I have already done to improve plugins in Wireshark) but it is odd and actually very inconsiderate in my opinion that he would do that without even bothering to explain why.

3. @rknall chose to not participate any further in the discussion, fair enough. I have no issue with that.

I am not sure what that represents as far as agreement goes but whatever, I appreciate your response.

My concern are the changes affecting plugin install paths, plugin file names and changes to the API that require work of people maintaining external plugins.

I would be OK with reverting only the changes that create extra work. I would also be OK with extending the plugin API with calls to add optional data without having to update old external plugins' source code.

I did not have time to prepare such rework, hence I proposed the reversion of the interconnected changes and I'm sorry that it affects so much of your work.

Replacing a lot of registration boilerplate with a single line is not requireing more work. Among all the work they are already required to do anyway replacing a lot of boilerplate with a single macro will improve the experience for everyone in the future.

So you can´t justify it on technical grounds and no one in the community expressed any concerns on the mailing list about these changes. You are just speaking out of turn and misinformed.
If this is merged then #19523 should be closed too.

@geraldcombs Before the plugin redesign the `cloudtrail.dll` was installed to a path containing `${MAJOR_VERSION}.${MINOR_VERSION}`, too. You changed that line in f4e71562d09d52fccd63b1839afefdc500bfcc7a and I kept `couldtrail.dll` being installed to the ABI-independent location, thus I did not fully revert that.
I think keeping the `${MAJOR_VERSION}.${MINOR_VERSION}` as part of the path would be safer, but it is up to you.

Why is it safer? The design is not ABI independent. That is the whole point. Do you want to have a technical discussion or not?

Let's discuss safety. The old API uses `plugin_version`, `plugin_register`and `plugin_describe`. Three very common names.

The new API uses a single symbol `wireshark_load_module`. This is both more efficient and just as important safer against (accidental) collisions.

Falco plugins are loaded via https://github.com/falcosecurity/libs/blob/master/userspace/plugin/plugin_loader.c and need to conform to the checks. It might be a good idea to use the Falco plugin API version numbers in the file path or name, but any Wireshark version numbers are irrelevant here.

This discussions seem to be circling around always the same point. And I have to say, the tone used in the last comment is way off for my taste and opinion.

I would merge this revert and then pick the parts we can agree and commit them part-by-part. It should be more gradually and not a single big one, and also, if there are changes that will lead to breaks, those should be kept for 5.0 and not in between. 

So from me, please stop the discussions and commit it, so we can move on. The consensus - on the technical steering committee, as well as with the majority of Core developers in this discussion - seems to be, that this should move into the repo, and therefore I would like to merge it. Also, I do not think this is a Draft, it just needs the appropriate rebases and changes to be committed.

I will point out that your point about 5.0 is silly. It holds no particular significance, it never has, and there have always been "breaks", as you call them, between major releases. This is nothing compared to some other things that didn't raise an eyebrow. I have been involved with this project for 9 nine years, about as long as you, and I know perfectly well what I am talking about. If you want to introduce a new (silly IMO) rule for X.0 that is fine but it is absolutely not true that such a relatively minor break as removing an awkward component from the plugin path should be kept for 5.0.

It is also false that the discussion is "always circling" around the same point.

The MR was started on the premise that there were unanswered questions in the mailing list (there weren't) and there wasn't a "cost benefit" analysis, which after 3 months of silence I actually bothered to help Balint fill in in parts. Funny that no one bothered to analyze or discuss those important points that I helpfully contributed. Just got back a bunch of vague hand waving and poorly formulated policy arguments as usual.

> I do not think we need to revert the whole change. I actually like the way the new version check is implemented and think it is beneficial to a lot of users, because it will reduce the number of changes they have to make in order to update their version.

... jive with your statement that "breaking changes" should be kept for 5.0? Actually curious, because the version check is a clear API/ABI break. Maybe I misunderstood.

This is what @rbalint is talking about when he says the change "creates more work for users" and that is unacceptable. Right? Did I understand that correctly?

I wanted to stay away from this, but ok. Yes you are right, I am contradicting my original statement somewhat. But at the same time I am not interested in a discussion anymore. We have tried time and time again to have a valid discussion, and as I accept that also @rbalint did not react openly in some parts of it, it was your last statement and your continuous disrespect to us that finally let me gave up.

One more thing - and I might be overstepping here a little bit. The technical committee is not a useless exercise. It is something we discussed time and time again at numerous SharkFests. And it is a discussion we could also have lead in more detail on -core, I give you that. But at the same time, it is not our job to motivate you to participate in the project itself. You claim that you are separating the technical from the social side of the project, and I am fine with that. Running it costs money and there are multiple reasons why we need the other parts and why they need to have a say in things. That you cannot accept that is one thing and I respect you for your opinion. That you cannot accept the opinion of others is another thing and I cannot accept the disrespect. 

For me, this is the end of the line. I am not in any kind of mood to indulge anymore in discussions about the technical side of this change. It has been discussed and decided multiple times, the reasons - although not shared by you apparently - have been brought and a final decision has been made. At this point, I no longer am interested in leading or having any discussion about it, and will leave any further steps to the board of the foundation and @geraldcombs.
